entities.name: PMID:10728358
observations: Rabbit atrial terminal-crest study comparing neonatal, weanling, and adult preparations during postnatal maturation.
Terminal Cx43 gap-junction area increased about 3.5-fold from birth to adulthood, while lateral-wall Cx43 remained relatively stable.
Longitudinal impulse velocity increased about 2.4-fold, transverse velocity remained relatively invariant, and electrical anisotropy therefore increased.
The study supports correlation between Cx43 spatial redistribution and propagation anisotropy but does not establish causality.

entities.name: Cx43
observations: Cx43 gap junctions redistributed preferentially toward myocyte termini during postnatal maturation in rabbit atrial terminal crest; total amount per myocyte changed little.
Terminal Cx43 redistribution was accompanied by faster longitudinal but not transverse impulse propagation.

entities.name: Atrial terminal crest
observations: Rabbit atrial terminal crest was studied across neonatal, weanling, and adult postnatal stages.
Maturation was associated with increased longitudinal conduction and electrical anisotropy alongside terminal enrichment of Cx43 gap junctions.

entities.name: Cx43-anisotropy correlation
observations: In postnatal rabbit atrial terminal crest, terminal Cx43 gap-junction area increased approximately 3.5-fold and longitudinal conduction velocity increased approximately 2.4-fold, while transverse velocity was relatively stable.

The concordant changes support a structure-function correlation in which preferential terminal Cx43 coupling accompanies increased longitudinal conductance and anisotropy; total Cx43 density was not the main changing variable.
